content: Simulate a moderately dense debris flow with shear-thinning non-Newtonian material. Please refer to Case2.jpg for geometry. Use debris density of 1700 kg/m^3, initial particle spacing dp = 0.5 m, use Symplectic step algorithm, artificial viscosity 0.1, output time interval 0.2s and run to total time 10s.

================================================================
  SIMULATION PLAN
================================================================

### Reasoning
I interpreted the sketch as a 3D rectangular flume of length 100 m, width 20 m, and wall height 40 m, with an initial debris reservoir occupying the last 15 m in x and filled up to 30 m height. The internal barrier was taken from the top/front views as a 4 m streamwise thickness, 14 m span across y, and 10 m height, leaving 3 m clearance to the front and back side walls. Since the image provides only approximate placement along x for the barrier, I placed it near the upstream half at x=12..16, consistent with the sketch. For rheology, I used a moderately dense shear-thinning debris flow: density 1700 kg/m^3, HBP_n=0.75 for shear-thinning, moderate consistency and yield stress, and artificial viscosity 0.1 as requested. The geometry XML is compatible with DualSPHysics GenCase; use Symplectic as the time integration algorithm in the execution section of the full case XML.

### Geometry XML
```xml
<geometry>
  <definition dp="0.5">
    <pointmin x="-1" y="-1" z="-1" />
    <pointmax x="101" y="21" z="41" />
  </definition>
  <commands>
    <mainlist>
      <setshapemode>dp | bound</setshapemode>
      <setdrawmode mode="full" />

      <!-- Initial debris reservoir at right end: 15 m long, full width 20 m, 30 m high -->
      <setmkfluid mk="0" />
      <drawbox>
        <boxfill>solid</boxfill>
        <point x="85" y="0" z="0" />
        <size x="15" y="20" z="30" />
      </drawbox>

      <!-- Main channel/tank boundaries: 100 m long, 20 m wide, 40 m high, open top -->
      <setmkbound mk="0" />
      <drawbox>
        <boxfill>bottom | left | right | front | back</boxfill>
        <point x="0" y="0" z="0" />
        <size x="100" y="20" z="40" />
        <layers vdp="0,1,2" />
      </drawbox>

      <!-- Internal barrier near upstream side: 4 m long (x), 14 m wide (y), 10 m high (z) -->
      <!-- From sketch: 3 m offset from front/back walls, so y = 3..17; placed near x = 12..16 -->
      <setmkbound mk="1" />
      <drawbox>
        <boxfill>solid</boxfill>
        <point x="12" y="3" z="0" />
        <size x="4" y="14" z="10" />
      </drawbox>

      <shapeout file="" />
    </mainlist>
  </commands>
</geometry>
```

### Physics Parameters
  gravity_z            = -9.81
  rhop0                = 1700.0
  coefh                = 1.0
  cflnumber            = 0.2
  phase_rhop           = 1700.0
  visco_nn             = 0.15
  tau_yield            = 0.02
  HBP_m                = 20.0
  HBP_n                = 0.75
  Visco                = 0.1
  DensityDT            = 3
  DensityDTvalue       = 0.1
  TimeMax              = 10.0
  TimeOut              = 0.2

================================================================
A visualization of the particle configuration has been generated.
Approve, request changes, or ask a question:

Two problems with the barrier. First, its thickness along the flow direction should be 2, not 4 — see the "2" label above it in the front view. Second, its streamwise position is wrong: in the front view the "60" dimension is measured from the right face of the barrier to the left face of the fluid block, so with the fluid occupying the last 15 m of the tank, the barrier sits much further downstream than where you placed it. Re-derive its x position from that dimension chain.

Fixed.

Barrier is now:
- thickness in x: 2 m
- position in x: 23 to 25 m

Reasoning:
- fluid block starts at x = 85 m
- given 60 m from barrier right face to fluid left face
- barrier right face = 85 - 60 = 25 m
- with 2 m thickness, barrier left face = 23 m

The rebuilt GenCase output is consistent with this update:
- barrier particle block present as a separate boundary mk
- total particles generated successfully
- build completed successfully

If that matches your intent, I can proceed to simulation.
